summary: Revised and requested re-execution of the shutdown probe after finding a sharper discriminator. The first run's trigger was timing dependent, so the revision raises the per-call completion window to 4000ms, issues 128 calls, interleaves Shutdown 2ms into the fill, and adds a post-shutdown phase that issues 8 calls of the same kind after Shutdown has returned. That phase has no race with the shutdown itself, and a construction run showed VerifyLeader leaving 3-5 of those 8 calls unanswered while Barrier and Apply answered all of them with the documented shutdown error — which the source explains: verifyCh is buffered with 64 slots (api.go 576) so its send case is ready with no receiver, while applyCh is unbuffered unless BatchApplyCh is enabled (api.go 549), so the apply path can only take the shutdown case. A new source range records that asymmetry, and the four comparisons separate the verify strand, the Barrier and Apply contrasts, and the no-shutdown control. No observation is claimed until the clean-copy receipt exists; adding a BatchApplyCh case to confirm the buffering mechanism remains unfinished.
